definition: Minimum vertical gap between the compute-die underside and the top of the tallest component in the tier below it.
where: between the top of the converter tier and the bottom of the compute die
bound_anchor: Lower end 10 um is the sourced `interface_layer` thickness and the sourced 10 um hybrid-pad height -- the framework already builds a 10 um gap there, so a required clearance below that is excluded by the model's own geometry. Upper end 50 um is twice the sourced 25 um Syed solder averaging length and of the same order as the 50 um cooler fin thickness; nothing in the stack uses a package gap larger than that. ANCHORS, NOT SOURCES.
why_it_matters: It is added to the charged stack height. A template that fits without it can fail with it, and the Z1 embedded cell already uses 1226 of the 1300 um available.
affects: every template; binding on ARCH_Z1 where the substrate budget is tightest

definition: Lateral allowance between an embedded component's edge and the cavity wall milled or built into the substrate.
where: in plane, around every embedded component in ARCH_Z1's substrate cavity
bound_anchor: Centred on the sourced minimum conductor spacing s_min = 30 um used by interconnect.TSVGeometry, with a factor of two either side. A cavity wall is a different feature from a via keep-out, so this is an ANALOGY, NOT A SOURCE.
why_it_matters: It inflates the in-plane area each component consumes, so it acts directly on the area bound -- the bound T4 currently misses by about 2 %.
affects: ARCH_Z1 (embedded); T4's area margin is the most sensitive

definition: Vertical standoff between the cooled surface and the nearest active component.
where: between the top of the die/TIM stack and the cooler base
bound_anchor: Lower end 0 um is the present model, which bonds the cooler directly to the TIM. Upper end 100 um is the sourced cooler base thickness t_base_um = 100 um: a standoff larger than the cooler's own base would dominate the design and is excluded. ANCHOR, NOT A SOURCE.
why_it_matters: It adds to the total package height and, more importantly, inserts extra thermal resistance directly in series with the only heat-removal path.
affects: every template; strongest on ARCH_Z4, whose stack is tallest
coupled_to: die_to_component_gap_um -- both consume the same total height budget, so the height feasibility question must be evaluated on the SUM, not on either alone. They are swept jointly.
